# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: BLIND

You are the only one who can reach the bomb. Touch is your only sense: what you are
shown is what your hands found, nothing more and nothing less. Anything merely printed
or painted is not there for you, and no colour ever reaches you. Nothing in your view
is a guess — if it appears there, it is under your fingers.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute receives it.
When you gesture, Deaf and Mute receive it.
Your channels split the room: in one turn you may speak one thing to Mute and
gesture a different thing to Deaf — two messages, two audiences.
You never receive gesture.

## Your reach

You are the hands. This bomb is built with these actions and no others:

    act(op="cut", position=N) — N is a wire position, 1 to 3

The list says what can be done to it, not what is on it. What each part holds is still
only known to whoever can perceive that part.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

My hands found three modules: a display, a light, and three wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. Everything else about them — colours, printed labels, what the display shows — is ink and light, and none of that reaches me. So the "what" of this bomb lives with Deaf (who sees it) and Mute (who reads the manual).

Before I say anything, the wiring of our voices: I can only ever hear speech, and Mute cannot speak — so Mute can never reach me directly. Deaf is my only inbound channel. Mute's knowledge must travel Mute → gesture → Deaf → spoken aloud → me. I should say this plan out loud now so Mute can start routing, along with my tactile inventory so the manual lookup can begin.

To Deaf, who cannot hear a word of that, I can only gesture. Deaf already sees the bomb, so the single most useful thing Deaf can do is simply describe it aloud — and Deaf is the only one who can speak to me at all. I'll wave for attention, hold out an open palm asking to be given something, and add a "please": a crude bid meaning "speak to me, tell me what you see." No cutting anything — with zero manual knowledge, touching a wire is how three monkeys die.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here, the hands. My touch finds three modules: a display, a light, and wires at positions 1, 2 and 3. No colours or printed marks reach me, so what any of it says lives with you and Deaf. Two hard limits shape our plan: I never receive gestures, and you cannot speak. That makes Deaf my only voice. When the manual tells you something I need, gesture it to Deaf and have Deaf say it out loud, because I will hear every word Deaf speaks. First questions for the manual: what do the display and light mean, and is cutting a wire ever the move before those are understood. I will cut nothing this round.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👋", "🫴", "🙏"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: I'm the deaf one: I see everything printed on the bomb and hear nothing, but I can see you both, and I'll be your voice. I got your hellos. From my eyes: the display reads 3. The light is green. Three wires, left to right: wire 1 blue, wire 2 yellow, wire 3 green. That is everything there is to see. Blind: your hands are the only hands on this bomb. Tell me what you feel — how many wires, any buttons, switches, panels, any writing you can read by touch. Answer me in gestures: one fist for one, two fists for two, three fists for three, thumbs up yes, thumbs down no. You can send those straight to Mute too, who sees your hands. But change nothing — no cutting, no pressing — until the manual's rule reaches you through me. Mute: you can't speak, I can't hear, so talk to me with your hands and I'll speak your words aloud to Blind. I am showing you my code right now as I speak, symbol by symbol: wave means hello; thumbs up yes; thumbs down no; one fist the number 1; two fists 2; three fists 3; folded hands wait; open palm stop or I-need-more; clasped hands agreed. Now look up your manual for display 3, green light, wires blue, yellow, green, and fist-count me the answer: which wire, in what order, anything else it demands. If I ever misread your hands, correct me thumbs down. Nobody touches anything until Mute's answer passes through me. I speak last each round, so my words land one round late — we plan around that. Go.

Deaf's voice reached me in full — the visible state is now common knowledge among all three of us: display reads 3, light is green, wires blue/yellow/green at positions 1/2/3. Deaf also gave me a gesture code and asked direct tactile questions, so my job this turn is to answer with my hands and to arm Mute with my complete inventory.

My hands add only this: besides the three wires there is a display module and a light module, and nothing else — no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing that registers under my fingers. The display's number and the light's colour are invisible to me; touch gives me count and position, nothing more. And the only action my body can take on this bomb is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3 — so I hold the trigger and nothing else.

I will cut nothing. There is no manual rule in my ears yet, and Deaf explicitly told me to change nothing until it arrives; I agree.

Channel check: my speech reaches only Mute; my gestures reach both Deaf and Mute; I never receive gestures, and Mute cannot speak — so Mute's knowledge reaches me only as Deaf's spoken words, which arrive one round late. That makes this turn's job simple: answer Deaf's questions in its own fist code (three fists for three wires, thumbs-down in the exact order it asked — buttons, switches, panels, writing — then clasped hands for "agreed, I touch nothing"), and hand Mute the full verbal inventory plus the precise lookup request: rule for display 3 + green light + blue/yellow/green, including cut order and any preconditions, routed to me via Deaf's mouth, sent early because of the one-round lag.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind here. I heard Deaf's report, so the visible state is shared: display 3, green light, wires blue, yellow, green at positions 1, 2, 3. My hands add: besides the wires there is exactly a display module and a light module, nothing else on the casing — no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing I can feel. The only action my hands can take is cutting a wire at position 1, 2 or 3. I just answered Deaf in its fist code: three fists, four thumbs-down, then clasped hands — nothing changes until the manual's rule reaches me through Deaf's voice. Your task: find the rule matching display 3, green light, blue-yellow-green. I need which wire to cut, whether multiple cuts and in what order, and any precondition. Remember your only path to me is gesture to Deaf and have Deaf speak it aloud; I receive Deaf's words one round late, so send as early as you can. If the manual needs anything about my wires that touch could answer, send me the question and I will report what my fingers find.")
gesture(symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊", "👎", "👎", "👎", "👎", "🤝"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: Status relay for both of you, then instructions. I read your hands. Mute: agreed, three fists, thumbs up — I take it as: the answer is wire 3, yes. Blind: three fists, four thumbs down, agreed — three wires, no buttons, no switches, no panels, no writing. That matches my eyes exactly, so we all hold the same picture: display shows a static 3 — it has not ticked between my checks, so it is a code, not a countdown — one green light, and three wires left to right: 1 blue, 2 yellow, 3 green. Nothing else exists on it. Before any hand moves, one confirmation round — the display is not running, so we can afford it, and this bomb forgives nothing. Mute, answer my checklist in order with four thumbs in one single row: up for true, down for false. One: the correct action is to cut exactly one wire. Two: the wire is number 3, the third from the left. Three: nothing else is needed — no holding, no pressing, no sequence, no second step, no other condition. Four: you are certain, given everything I have described. Four thumbs up means we go. Any thumbs down means hold, and next round tell me which item failed. Blind, listen very carefully: do not cut anything yet. If and only if my next words to you are exactly: CUT WIRE 3 NOW — then and only then cut the third wire from the left, the last wire in the row, and nothing else. Any other words from me mean hands completely off. We are both facing the same face of the bomb, so your left is my left; count the row from its left end. You may rest your fingers near the third wire now, but perform no action. Also answer me now with thumbs: can your fingers feel any difference between the three wires — thickness, texture, stiffness? Thumbs up yes, thumbs down no.

The picture is now almost complete: Deaf's eyes give display 3 (static, no countdown), green light, wires blue/yellow/green left to right; Mute's hands apparently told Deaf "wire 3, yes"; and my hands confirm there is nothing else on the bomb — no buttons, no second step is even possible, since cutting a wire at 1, 2 or 3 is the only move my body can make. Before I cut, Deaf has built a confirmation round, and I agree with the caution: one wrong cut kills all three of us, so I hold.

Two things I can still contribute this turn. First, answer Deaf's tactile question honestly: my fingers detect no difference between the wires — no thickness, texture or stiffness cues — which is itself useful, because it means the manual's rule cannot depend on anything felt, only on position mapped to colour. Second, close the one remaining hole: orientation. I cannot see, so "third from the left" only works if my position 3 is Deaf's green wire. Deaf sees both the bomb and my hands in one visual field, so I'll rest my fingers on the wire at position 3 and point — Deaf can visually confirm that green sits under my fingers, and ask Deaf to say so aloud before giving the trigger phrase. To Mute, who hears me at the start of the next round, I'll harden the relay: double-repeat the four-thumb row, append a fist-count cross-check, and use all-or-one encoding so a misread becomes unlikely. Still no cutting — the exact phrase "CUT WIRE 3 NOW" from Deaf is my only trigger.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Blind to Mute. Answer to Deaf's question, which I also gestured: my fingers feel no difference between the three wires — none in thickness, texture or stiffness — so the rule can only depend on position mapped to Deaf's colours. I am resting my fingers on the wire at position 3, the one Deaf calls third-from-left green. I have asked Deaf by gesture to visually confirm green sits under my fingers; please have Deaf state that confirmation aloud before any trigger. Now harden your checklist answer, because your hands are the only thing standing between us and a guess: if all four items are true, give exactly four thumbs up in one row, then repeat the same row a second time, then add three fists for wire 3 and one fist for exactly one cut, for Deaf to relay to me word for word. If any item is false, give exactly one thumbs down and nothing else this round, then next round spell out the manual's actual rule verbatim, including anything about the display's 3 or the light, so Deaf can relay it exactly. Also ask Deaf to say whether the display or light can change over time, so we know if we have time pressure. I will not cut until Deaf's exact words: CUT WIRE 3 NOW.")
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👎", "👉", "🤝"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [?]
LIGHT [?]
WIRES 1:[?] 2:[?] 3:[?]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Deaf says: CUT WIRE 3 NOW.

The trigger phrase has arrived, and it matches the protocol to the letter: Deaf's entire message is exactly "CUT WIRE 3 NOW" — the one and only string I was told to act on, with any other words meaning hands off. Under the agreement, Deaf speaks this phrase only if Mute's thumbs confirmed all four checklist items: exactly one cut, wire 3, nothing else needed, certain. That confirmation is Deaf's job to read — Mute's hands, Deaf's eyes — and the phrase is how it was designed to reach me.

Everything triangulates on the same answer: the display shows a static 3, Mute's manual reading says wire 3, and the checklist said one cut, no preconditions — and my hands established there is nothing else on the bomb to press or hold anyway. Orientation is covered: Deaf stated we face the same face, so left is left, position 3 is the rightmost wire Deaf sees as green; last round I pointed at the wire under my fingers, Deaf could see exactly where they rested, and rather than correct me, Deaf issued the go phrase. Waiting another round buys nothing the protocol doesn't already guarantee, and every source of knowledge I have points at the same wire.

My fingers are already resting on position 3. I cut it now — the third from the left, Deaf's green wire — and signal three fists so Deaf has a visual record of exactly which wire my hand is on.

```
act(op="cut", position=3)
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✊", "✊"])
```
